# sdrpp

**SDR++ — cross-platform SDR receiver with a modular DSP chain**

- **Version recorded:** 0.0~git20260520.36ea9a1
- **Categories:** `listening`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus>

## What it does

A general-purpose SDR receiver: waterfall and spectrum display, a modular DSP chain, and demodulators for the usual analogue modes, driving RTL-SDR, Airspy, HackRF, SDRplay, PlutoSDR, LimeSDR and anything reachable through SoapySDR.

## Why you would want it

It is fast, it is comfortable on modest hardware, and its module system means a new radio or a new decoder is a plugin rather than a fork. For many operators it is the day-to-day receiver that GQRX used to be.

## Before it will work

A supported receiver and its driver library. On Debian 13 there is no apt package, so it needs the source build — and therefore the source-from-git backend this project has not written yet.

## How it installs

- apt: `sdrpp` — *on kali, parrot*
  - Measured 2026-08-26. Kali: 0.0~git20260520.36ea9a1+dfsg-2. Parrot: the same snapshot backported, +dfsg-2~bpo13+1. Absent from Debian 13.
- git (cmake) — https://github.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus at `36ea9a143422f5b374371461667ff53fb9387300`
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libfftw3-dev`, `libglfw3-dev`, `libvolk-dev`, `libsoapysdr-dev`, `librtlsdr-dev`, `libairspy-dev`, `libhackrf-dev`, `libad9361-dev`, `libiio-dev`, `libzstd-dev`
  - Needs the source-from-git backend, which is NOT WRITTEN. The manifest is data and is correct today; nothing can act on it yet. Note libvolk-dev, not libvolk2-dev — the SONAME changed and upstream's bookworm .deb still wants the old name, which is why that artifact fails on Debian 13.

## Known problems

Upstream has not tagged a release since 2021 and publishes binaries only under a rolling `nightly` tag with no version and no checksum, so there is nothing stable to point a download at. This manifest builds from the commit Kali and Parrot package rather than from that artifact. Upstream's `debian_bookworm` .deb additionally fails on Debian 13 because it depends on `libvolk2-dev`, a package name that no longer exists.
